title: Cohort-anchored Traffic Conductor with Variant Sculpting and Automated Failsafe
author: Jordan E. Lin
commit_summary: Initial implementation of Traffic Conductor core loop; variant sculpting strategy; deterministic rollback reason codes; session-affinity-preserving phased drain; decayed shadowing implementation; telemetry gates and rehearsal mode; integration tests and docs updates
description:
Context and motivation: We need a unified conductor that lets product teams express cohort-anchored traffic phasing policies (canary, A/B, and shadowing) with automated failsafe behavior tied to deterministic rollback reasons so operators can reason about regressions. Current rollout primitives are fragmented across the orchestration layer and the legacy traffic proxy; recovery semantics are ad-hoc and hard to audit. This PR introduces a first-class Traffic Conductor that centralizes policy evaluation, variant sculpting (fractional shaping per cohort), and deterministic failsafe triggers (latency/accuracy/telemetry anchors) so model swaps and experiments run with predictable rollback behavior.

What this PR does (high level): Implements a policy-driven conductor that: 1) assigns cohorts to variant lanes and sculpts traffic fractions using a decay-aware allocator so small cohorts do not overshoot; 2) preserves session affinity during phased drains to avoid user-facing churn; 3) supports decayed shadowing (shadow traffic that ramps down automatically as signatures stabilize) to reduce cost during long-running experiments; 4) surfaces deterministic rollback reason codes (e.g., SLO_LATENCY, REGRESSION_ACCURACY, TELEMETRY_DROP) and stores them in the rollout journal for audit and replay; 5) adds a "rehearsal" playback mode that replays sampled production traffic against candidate variants prior to increasing live traffic; 6) implements telemetry gates that tie to existing metrics pipelines (via MetricsProxy hook) and allow multi-metric gating with configurable windows.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc in Linear (ENG-4123) and architecture updates (docs/architecture/rollout-variants.md)
- [x] Core conductor loop with deterministic reason codes
- [x] Variant sculptor algorithm + unit tests
- [x] Session-affinity drain hooks integrated with proxy adapter
- [x] Rehearsal mode + small-scale playback harness for safety
- [x] e2e integration test that simulates noisy cohorts
- [x] Runbook and console timeline UI updates (docs/runbooks/traffic-conductor.md and console component)

Summary of commits: commit 1: traffic_conductor core loop and state machine; commit 2: variant_sculptor algorithm + tests; commit 3: telemetry gate hooks and deterministic rollback codes; commit 4: rehearsal and playback harness; commit 5: console timeline + cohort selector UI; commit 6: docs and runbook; commit 7: integration tests and CI fixes.

Files touched (high level): see changed_files field for the most relevant placements. Changes are intentionally localized: the conductor lives under pkg/orchestrator with adapter interfaces for the proxy and metrics layers. Helm values add rollout tuning knobs and safe-default SLO thresholds. Console changes add a timeline and action buttons for manual revoke/promote.

Review conversation (highlights):
- Priya Sharma (reviewer): "Overall architecture LGTM. A couple of questions: what guarantees do we provide around exact fractional splits for cohorts with very low p95 traffic? Suggest making the sculptor deterministic per cohort seed so tests are reproducible."
- Author (Jordan): "Answered: sculptor uses a seeded PRNG derived from cohort id + rollout id; added deterministic tests to controller_test.go. Also included a 'minimum-commit' policy to avoid flapping for tiny cohorts."
- Diego M. Rivera (reviewer): "Telemetry gates look good; can we make the gating window pluggable? Also add a metric tag to the rollback journal entry so we can correlate with dashboards."
- Author: "Done — gating window is a config flag and rollback journal now emits metric_tag (rollout_id:cohort). Added an e2e that triggers TELEMETRY_DROP and validates journal entry."
- Ellen K. Morris (approver): "Approved after small nits; asked to add a short paragraph to the runbook describing when to use rehearsal vs. direct canary."

CI summary: initial pipeline failed lint on console TS types (fixed), unit flakiness in TestSculptorNoise resolved by adjusting RNG seed (reliable now), integration e2e passed in staging with synthetic cohorts. Final pipeline: build pass, unit tests pass, integration pass, lint pass. CI badge: pass.

Merge notes and outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-03-03 after approvals. Release notes entry created under Release v5.8: "Introduce Traffic Conductor (cohort-anchored phasing, variant sculpting, rehearsal playback, deterministic rollback codes) — opt-in via helm rolloutValues. See docs/runbooks/traffic-conductor.md for runbook and migration steps."

Operational considerations: This feature is gated behind a helm flag rollout.conductor.enabled=false by default. Encouraged path: enable in staging, run rehearsal for key models, then enable canary phasing. The conductor emits rollout_journal entries that are indexed in the observability pipeline (alertable) so SRE can build fatality thresholds.

Backward compatibility: Existing simple traffic splits continue to work. The conductor registers a compatibility adapter so teams can opt-in gradually. No breaking API changes.
release_notes: Introduce Traffic Conductor: cohort-anchored phasing, variant sculpting, rehearsal playback mode, deterministic rollback reason codes. Opt-in via helm rollout.conductor.enabled. See docs/runbooks/traffic-conductor.md for migration steps.
notes_for_release_manager: Feature gated; recommend staged rollout in staging followed by canary with rehearsal. Update SRE dashboards to surface rollback reason codes (TELEMETRY_DROP, SLO_LATENCY, REGRESSION_ACCURACY).
qa_checklist: Unit tests for sculptor algorithm; integration e2e simulating cohort noise; smoke test for session affinity preservation; rehearsal mode replay verification; rollout_journal indexing verified in staging
post_merge_tasks: Monitor rollout_journal for first 48h, coordinate with SRE to add alert for TELEMETRY_DROP >= 2 in 30m window, schedule internal demo for platform teams
user_impact: Opt-in. No immediate user-facing changes until rollout.conductor.enabled=true and a policy is created. When enabled, safer canaries and lower-cost shadowing for long experiments.
repro_instructions: Enable helm value rollout.conductor.enabled=true in a staging cluster, create a RolloutPolicy (examples in docs/runbooks/traffic-conductor.md), run rehearsal with sample traffic and verify rollout_journal entries and console timeline updates.
